quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway, what should they do?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end soon. All traffic in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: When must children wear seat belts?

options.text: Anytime they are in a moving car.
Only if their parents say they should.
Only if they weigh under 100 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anytime they are in a moving car.
questions.explanation: The law requires all children under 18 to wear fastened seat belts in all moving vehicles, no matter where they sit in the car.

questions.question: If you crash into an unattended vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can leave without trying to find the owner.
You must contact the owner or leave a note.
You must stay near the vehicle until the owner comes.
You should call a tow truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must contact the owner or leave a note.
questions.explanation: If you crash into an unattended vehicle, try to find the owner and tell them. If you cannot find them, leave a note with your name, phone number, and license plate number.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clean.
Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead of you.
Be careful around all other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your distance from other vehicles because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They become better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things struggle to stay in their lanes and control their vehicles.

questions.question: When should you always signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic from an alley. Signals tell other drivers what you plan to do and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass by moving to the right side of the road and stopping. Do this whenever you see flashing lights or hear a siren, no matter which direction the vehicle is going. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn how the vehicle works before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn how the vehicle works before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes finding and understanding the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shifter, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: When can you use flashing hazard lights?

options.text: When your vehicle is stopped or broken down on the highway or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle is stopped or broken down on the highway or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use flashing hazard lights only when your vehicle is broken down or legally stopped on the highway or shoulder. You can also use them in a funeral procession.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It makes you feel more confident than you should.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol weakens the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your balance, and makes it hard to judge distance. This makes it dangerous to drive.

questions.question: What can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Leaving extra time to reach your destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: Why should you signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving the curb?

options.text: Only when other cars are nearby.
It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only while you are making the move, not before.
Not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. The law requires this. Always signal before leaving the curb so other drivers know your plan.

questions.question: How should you pass a bicycle on a two-lane road without bike lanes?

options.text: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming. Then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must move out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic light or stop sign to pass.
Honk to warn the cyclist that you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming. Then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicycle the same way you pass another vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist. On faster roads or with groups of cyclists, leave at least 5 feet. Honking can startle riders and cause accidents.

questions.question: When can you drive in a lane with a red X signal?

options.text: If you don't see oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Lane signals show which lanes are open or closed. A red X means the lane is closed. Never drive in a lane with a red X.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to clear before moving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a sharp turn ahead. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Understand that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Avoid looking at passengers, searching for items, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. If another driver looks distracted, stay farther away. Distracted drivers cause more accidents.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when the other lane is clear and safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Change how you drive when weather changes suddenly.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you during bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes. Slow down in rain and fog. Pay attention to vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the weather.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and take out the key.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Where is passing not allowed?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These areas are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Go through and make the other vehicle stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic controls, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let that vehicle pass safely before you go.

questions.question: How should a seat belt fit?

options.text: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
So the warning light does not turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should rest comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When should you slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, on sharp curves you cannot see around, where pedestrians are present, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: How do you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Do not drive next to them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop when you see a red octagonal sign.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Continue to the next exit, then safely turn around and go back.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. This is the law. Do not skip signaling just because you do not see other cars.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the same full lane width as all other vehicles. This is important for safe riding.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road ahead is closed to traffic.
The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction and maintenance work ahead. These signs tell you to slow down and be extra careful as you approach the work zone.

questions.question: A steady green light at an intersection means that you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is safe. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic is blocking your view. You should:

options.text: Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before going ahead with your turn.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
Edge your car into each lane of opposing traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before going ahead with your turn.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Don't drink if you are going to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows that traffic can only go in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: After an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the risk of death in a crash increases. Driving faster than 80 miles per hour gives you almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may try risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic signals help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey these signals. However, when a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer's directions instead of the signal.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a greater crash risk when using which of these?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone (even hands-free) or any audio device (radio or CD player) can distract you and increase your crash risk.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop:

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or too close for safe crossing. If you are not sure, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your brain activity and hurts your driving skills. Drinking reduces reaction time and impairs judgment.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit before driving. Buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs before you start the car.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: If a car is tailgating you on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Speed up to match the other car's speed.
Move right to let the car pass.
Slow down but stay in your lane.
Let them pass and then tailgate them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move right to let the car pass.
questions.explanation: On a multilane highway, move to the right lane when it is safe to let the tailgating car pass. The left lane is for faster vehicles passing slower ones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: A sign with this shape and color is a ____ sign.
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs like this are only used to warn of no passing zones.
